definition: Assigning a label to an entire video clip — the video analogue of image classification.
details: Assigning a label to an entire video clip — the video analogue of image classification. Spatiotemporal CNNs and video transformers drive benchmarks like Kinetics.

explainer.lead: Video Classification assigns a label to an entire video clip — the video analogue of image classification. It matters as a core benchmark task for recognizing what a clip shows as a whole.

tiers.eli5: It's like sorting home videos into folders by what they're about, one label per whole clip.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use spatiotemporal CNNs and video transformers, evaluated on benchmarks like Kinetics. The pitfall is that a single label for the whole clip leaves no room for events that change over time.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as assigning a label to an entire video clip, the video analogue of image classification, with spatiotemporal CNNs and video transformers driving benchmarks such as Kinetics. No formulas or numeric limits are specified.

explainer.example: A model watches a clip and outputs one label for the whole thing, scored against the Kinetics benchmark.
